cards.text: Saul, Israel's new king, has just been confirmed as king at Gilgal, and Saul and all the men of Israel are rejoicing. Then Samuel, the prophet who's been leading Israel, stands up in front of all Israel. He tells them he listened to everything they said, and he set a king over them.

cards.question: Samuel points to the new king walking before them. Then he talks about himself. How does Samuel describe himself?

cards.text: Then Samuel puts his whole record on trial, right there before the LORD and His anointed. Friend, if I tried that, the dead batteries I shared that drawer with would STILL be lined up to complain.

cards.question: Samuel asks the people if he ever took anyone's ox or donkey, cheated anyone or took a bribe. If he did, what does he promise to do?
When Samuel asks, the people say he cheated or oppressed some of them.

cards.text: Samuel says the LORD and His anointed are witnesses that nobody found anything in his hand, and the people agree. Friend, that's a cleaner record than my apron has EVER had.
Then Samuel flips it around. Now he's going to confront them before the LORD with all the righteous acts the LORD has done for them and their fathers.

cards.question: Samuel starts back when Jacob went to Egypt and the fathers cried out to the LORD. The LORD sent them Moses and ___.

cards.text: Moses and Aaron brought the fathers out of Egypt and settled them right here in this place. Now they've got a home, friend.

cards.question: Once the fathers are settled in the land, they forget the LORD their God.

cards.text: So He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines and the king of Moab. Sisera, the Philistines AND Moab is not a rough week, friend, that's a whole rough lineup.

cards.question: Under all that pressure, the fathers cry out to the LORD. What do they confess?

answers.text: They had mocked the LORD's prophets
They had robbed the LORD's altar

cards.text: They admit they served the Baals and Ashtoreths and ask Him to deliver them so they can serve Him. So the LORD sends deliverers, and Samuel names them: Jerubbaal, Barak, Jephthah and one more.

cards.question: The last deliverer Samuel names is himself.
The LORD delivered them from their enemies on every side, and they dwelt ___.

cards.text: Then Samuel brings it right up to now. When Nahash, king of the Ammonites, moved against them, they told Samuel no, they had to have a king.

cards.question: Samuel says they demanded a king even though they already had one. Who does Samuel say was already their king?

cards.text: Here's the king they chose, the one they requested, and the LORD has placed him over them. That's the ding on your phone, friend: the thing you ordered is ON the porch.

cards.question: Samuel lays out an if. If the people and their king fear the LORD, serve Him, obey His voice and follow Him, Samuel says all will be well.
But if they disobey and rebel, Samuel says the hand of the LORD will be ___ them, just like with their fathers.

cards.text: Then Samuel tells them to watch a great thing the LORD will do before their eyes. And he asks them, "Is it not the wheat harvest today?"

cards.question: It's the wheat harvest, and Samuel says he'll call on the LORD to send something. What?
Samuel says the thunder and rain will make the people know and see something. What?

answers.text: The evil of asking for a king
The strength of their new king
The LORD's care for their fields

cards.text: Samuel calls to the LORD, and that same day the LORD sends thunder and rain. You finally get a sunny day off, you step outside, and the sky goes BOOM.

cards.question: When the thunder and rain come, all the people greatly ___ the LORD and Samuel.

cards.text: They beg Samuel to pray to the LORD his God for them so they won't die, and they admit they've added the evil of asking for a king to all their sins. Friend, that's me when the smoke alarm goes off: suddenly I'm confessing EVERY burnt batch I ever made.

cards.question: Samuel answers the scared crowd. What does he tell them first?
Samuel tells the people that after all this evil, they should stop following the LORD.

cards.text: Instead, he says, serve the LORD with all your heart, and don't turn aside after worthless things that can't profit you or deliver you, because they're empty. Empty, friend, like a cookie box that looks GREAT until you open the lid.

cards.question: Samuel promises the LORD will not abandon His people, for the sake of His great name. What other reason does he give?

answers.text: He was pleased to make them His own
They promised to serve Him from now on
They finally have a king to lead them

cards.question: Then Samuel talks about himself. He says it would be a sin against the LORD to stop ___ for the people.

cards.text: He'll keep teaching them the good and right way, too. Then comes his "Above all": fear the LORD, serve Him faithfully with all your heart, and consider the great things He has done for them.

cards.question: Samuel ends with a warning: if the people persist in doing evil, only their king will be swept away.

findings.problem: The joke says that if Papa Dorin put his record on trial, the drawer batteries would line up to complain. That implies Samuel's record would come out clean, which gives away card 5 (the people say Samuel did not cheat or oppress them).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory fact: the dead batteries in the drawer have complaints about Papa Dorin. The backstory only has the batteries arguing over who has the most charge, and Papa Dorin welcoming every newcomer. The drawer is not his bakery, so the allowance for made-up small moments doesn't cover it.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Jacob and Moses appear here for the first time in the lesson without being identified.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The punchline "is not a rough week, friend, that's a whole rough lineup" contrasts a week with a lineup. Those aren't the same kind of thing, so the joke doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Jerubbaal, Barak and Jephthah are named without saying who they are. Most bakers won't know that Jerubbaal is Gideon.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The statement applies fear, serve, obey and follow to both the people and the king, and it is marked True. In 1 Samuel 12:14, fearing, serving, obeying and not rebelling are said of "you" (the people). Only following the LORD is said of "both you and the king."

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The opening card tells and cites 1 Samuel 11:15, which is in the previous passage. That passage is provided "for context only. It is not part of the lesson." The stop's range is 1 Samuel 12:1-11, but the card's citation reaches outside it.
findings.question: May an opening story card retell and cite verses from the previous passage (provided for context only) when it sets the scene? If so, should the card's citation include those verses even though they fall outside the stop's verse range?
